title: What's Your Purpose? When to Raise It, When to Let Go
coreMove: Choose a conversation only when its honest purpose is something that conversation can actually produce.
sourcePressure: The chapter asks whether to raise the conversation at all by sorting legitimate purposes from warning-sign purposes and distinguishing letting go from suppression.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Raising every grievance because honesty sounds virtuous.

sourceAnchors.name: the three legitimate purposes and three warning-sign purposes
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sorts learning, expressing, and problem-solving from making the other person suffer, winning, and changing character.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A purpose that a conversation cannot produce should not be allowed to design the conversation.

sourceAnchorsNote: No chapter-specific real named anecdote, study, or researcher was available in the source sidecars for this chapter. Source anchors are traceable framework artifacts or edition/context facts only; do not invent named studies or reuse the source-banned Jack-Michael, Sydney, or author-family examples.
